review.brief_reason: Both the inner and outer changes only merge products of square roots into a single square root: sqrt(E)sqrt(F)sqrt(G) -> sqrt(EFG) inside the cosine, and sqrt(A)sqrt(B)sqrt(C)sqrt(D) -> sqrt(ABCD) for the outer denominator. Every radicand is of the form (sin/cos)^2+1 or 1+positive/((cos)^2+1), hence strictly >=1 for all real x1, so the radicands are positive and sqrt multiplicativity sqrt(x)sqrt(y)=sqrt(xy) is exact under ordinary real semantics. The cosine argument and all decimal constants and the single variable x1 are unchanged; no denominator can vanish in either form, so the domain (all reals) is preserved.
